How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 2, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, July 2, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Chan
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Harrington

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. PARKS MAKE LIFE BETTER MONTH

  B. LA COUNTY ASSESSOR PRESENTATION

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of June 18, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 2, 2024  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. FIRST AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  ARCHITECTURAL RESOURCES GROUP (ARG) FOR PREPARATION OF
  HISTORIC RESOURCES SURVEY PHASE 2

  The Community Development Department is requesting a First Amendment to
  an existing professional services agreement with Architectural Resources Group
  (ARG) for preparation of a citywide historic resources survey. On October 3,
  2023, the City Council approved the Professional Services Agreement with ARG
  and authorized the City Manager to execute said agreement and issue a
  purchase order in the amount of $40,000. The project is nearing completion,
  but additional time is needed for the full completion of the survey report and
  district maps. No additional funds are requested as part of this term extension.
  Funds have already been allocated as part of Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the First Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with
  Architectural Resources Group (ARG) to extend the term of the agreement
  till December 3, 2024; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment.

  D. ACCEPTANCE OF GRANT FROM ASSEMBLYMEMBER FONG’S OFFICE,
  AGREEMENT WITH LA CASA DE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY CENTER TO
  INCLUDE APPROVAL OF IMPROVEMENT PROJECT AND ACCEPTANCE OF
  NOTICE OF EXEMPTION [RESOLUTION NO. 24-16]

  The City was notified that it would be receiving targeted state funding on behalf
  of La Casa de San Gabriel Community Center. As the recipient and administrator
  of the funds, the City has developed an agreement with La Casa to ensure
  proper compliance with the requirements of the grant. For the administration
  of the La Casa grant, La Casa will pay for the received services and, through the
  City, will request reimbursement from the State agency. As with the similar

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 2, 2024  3
   grant for Friends of La Laguna, staff is recommending that the City forego
  collecting an administrative fee to oversee the grant.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The improvement
  projects to be completed at La Casa are exempt from the requirements of CEQA,
  per Guidelines 15331, Class 31, which applies to “projects limited to maintenance,
  repair, stabilization, rehabilitation, restoration, preservation, conservation or
  reconstruction of historical resources in a manner consistent with the Secretary
  of the Interior’s Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties with Guidelines
  for Preserving, Rehabilitating, Restoring, and Reconstructing Historic Buildings
  (1995), Weeks and Grimmer.”

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Accept the Grant from Assemblymember Fong’s Office on behalf of La Casa.

  2. Approve the agreement with La Casa and the improvement project with
  review by the Community Development Department, as necessary.

  3. Find the project is exempt from California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15331 and authorize the City Manager
  to file the attached Notice of Exemption.

  4. Authorize the City Manager to act as the authority on the City’s behalf.

  5. Adopt Resolution No. 24-16, required for the grant with La Casa.

  E. SERVICE AGREEMENT WITH CINTAS CORPORATION FOR UNIFORMS
  RENTALS, REPAIRS, AND LAUNDRY SERVICE FOR PUBLIC WORKS IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $26,400 ANNUALLY

  The Public Works Department requires all field staff to wear a City-issued
  uniform. In August 2019, the City entered into a five-year service agreement
  with Cintas Corporation to provide uniform services, including uniform rental,
  laundry, and repair for all field staff. The contract will expire on August 31, 2024.
  This item requests Council’s approval to enter a five-year Service Agreement
  with Cintas Corporation through OMNIA Partners, a nationwide cooperative
  purchasing organization. The cost of service will be $26,400 annually and is
  included in the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 2, 2024  4
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve a five-year Service Agreement
  with Cintas Corporation and authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase
  Order with Cintas Corporation for $26,400 annually using Field Operations
  Division budget account 121-800-02-43-000 for $19,200 and Sewer budget
  account 137-800-01-43-000 for $7,200.

  F. PURCHASE OF A FIRE DEPARTMENT STAFF VEHICLE NOT TO EXCEED THE
  BUDGETED AMOUNT OF $80,000

  The San Gabriel Fire Department utilizes a variety of vehicles in its fleet to meet
  emergency response and administrative responsibilities. The proposed new
  vehicle will replace a 2004 Chevrolet Tahoe that has more than 215,000 miles
  and has served as the primary emergency vehicle for the past five Fire Chiefs,
  Fire Prevention, and is currently assigned to a Division Chief. The total purchase
  price, including tax, documentation and delivery is not to exceed $80,000. The
  acquisition is included in the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 budget and funded in the
  Fleet Replacement Fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to issue a
  purchase order in an amount up to $80,000 to a dealership with a suitable
  vehicle as detailed in the Staff Report.

  G. APPROVAL OF FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 FIRE DEPARTMENT SUPPLIES AND
  EQUIPMENT OPEN PURCHASE ORDERS OF UP TO BUDGETED AMOUNTS
  $84,210 AND $65,000

  The San Gabriel Fire Department, during daily operations, maintains a supply
  of expendable items and durable equipment to fulfil its mission. Open purchase
  orders, renewed each Fiscal Year (FY) are used to keep the Department stocked
  with personal protective equipment, paramedic, and firefighting supplies,
  delivered on an as-needed basis. Vendors, reviewed regularly, are selected
  through competitive bid, piggyback and cooperative purchasing agreements.
  Paramedic and Firefighting equipment and supplies are budgeted for FY 2024-
  2025 as line items in the amount of $84,210 (Emergency Medical Service
  Supplies) and $65,000 (Personal Protective Equipment). Allocation for these

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 2, 2024  5
   purchases is made from the 121-761-00-21-000 account and are fully funded
  in the adopted budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the issuance of open
  purchase orders of up to the budgeted amounts of $84,210 for Life Assist, Inc.
  and of up to the budgeted amount of $65,000 to Municipal Emergency Services.
  All purchases are to be made pursuant to Title III, Section 34.35 of the San
  Gabriel Municipal Code, permitting the City to piggyback on a contract or
  cooperative purchasing agreement prepared by and processed through
  another local, state, or federal government agency.

  H. 2025 SAN GABRIEL LUNAR LANTERN FESTIVAL

  Since 2016, the City of San Gabriel has hosted a Lunar New Year Festival in the
  Mission District. For the 2025 event, celebrating the year of the Snake, staff
  proposes a two-day event with co-producer World Journal Los Angeles (WJLA)
  held on Saturday, February 1, from 12:00-9:00 pm and Sunday, February 2, from
  12:00-8:00 pm. Event costs will be covered by WJLA and associated sponsors.
  In-kind costs of staff time for street closures, public safety personnel, etc. will
  be covered by the City. Additionally, the costs of the welcome gathering for
  dignitaries, which is approximately $300, will be covered by the City. This cost
  constitutes a great savings from the $30,000 budget allocated for this event.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as a short two-day event
  will not have any foreseeable impacts on the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the proposal and draft the
  Professional Services Agreement to authorize World Journal Los Angeles to
  produce the 2025 Lunar Lantern Festival and authorize the City Manager to sign
  the final agreement.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 709 AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO EMERGENCY SHELTERS, GROUP

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 2, 2024  6
   HOMES, LOWER BARRIER NAVIGATION CENTER, SUPPORTIVE AND
  TRANSITIONAL HOUSING (ZTA24-003) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST
  READING

  The proposed Zone Text Amendment would amend Chapter 153 of the San
  Gabriel Municipal Code relating to Emergency Shelters, Group Homes,
  Lower Barrier Navigation Center, Supportive and Transitional Housing. The
  proposed Zone Text Amendment is intended to implement the goals and
  programs identified in the 2021-2029 Housing Element. The Fiscal Year
  2024-2025 Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal publication
  (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No. 121-702-
  00-22-000) of the ordinance, if adopted by the City Council.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). An initial Study/Negative Declaration (IS/ND) was
  prepared for the 2021-2029 Housing Element, as required by CEQA, Public
  Resources Code (PRC) Section 21000 et seq., the CEQA Guidelines, and the
  City of San Gabriel Local Guidelines for Implementing CEQA. The IS/ND
  considered the policies and programs outlined in the Housing Element. The
  Housing Element establishes the objectives, policies, and programs to assist
  the City in achieving state-mandated housing goals. No formal land use
  changes or physical development are proposed at this time and future land
  use and physical development would require separate environmental
  evaluation.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 709;

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 709 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE)
  OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO EMERGENCY
  SHELTERS, GROUP HOMES, LOWER BARRIER NAVIGATION CENTER,
  SUPPORTIVE AND TRANSITIONAL HOUSING.

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.
  The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 2, 2024  7
   6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PURCHASE OF AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE READER SYSTEM AND
  BALLISTIC HELMETS FROM FLOCK SAFETY AND PROFORCE LAW
  ENFORCEMENT UNDER 2021 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY GRANT
  PROGRAM IN THE AMOUNT OF $61,500 AND $57,920.79
  RESPECTIVELY

  The U.S. Department of Homeland Security provides funding to State and
  local governments through the State Homeland Security Program (SHSP).
  San Gabriel Police Department is allocated $119,354, which is exclusively
  dedicated to procurement of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) and
  Ballistic Helmets. The 2021 SHSP sub-recipient agreement and Resolution
  No. 23-21 were presented and approved by the City Council on May 2, 2023,
  which awarded the City $119,354 in grant funds. This program does not
  require matching funds from the City. The initial outlay of $119,354 for the
  ALPRs and Ballistic Helmets will be fully funded by the 2021 SHSP grant
  award. The deadline to use these funds is November 2024 and will be
  reimbursed within 120 days of the submission of a reimbursement request.
  In year 2 and onward, the annual subscription with FLOCK Safety for the
  ALPRs will be $60,000 per year, funded by the General Fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to
  purchase FLOCK Safety Automated License Plate Readers and PROFORCE
  Law Enforcement Ballistic Helmet equipment using the allocated State
  Homeland Security Program grant funding.

  B. GENERAL PLAN UPDATE DISCUSSION

  Under the provisions of Government Code Section 65300, each City and
  County shall prepare and adopt a comprehensive, long-term general plan
  for the physical development of a City and County. The general plan shall
  consist of a statement of development policies and include the following
  eight mandatory elements: land use, circulation, housing, conservation,
  open space, noise, safety, and environmental justice. The City of San Gabriel

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 2, 2024  8
   adopted it general plan in January 1990 and a comprehensive update in
  2004. There is no fiscal impact at this time.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss a potential general plan
  update and provide direction to staff to initiate a comprehensive update of
  the 2004 General Plan. This will allow the City to update all the mandated
  elements in the General Plan as well as add newly required elements. A
  comprehensive update will allow all the elements to be consistently current.
  A comprehensive update will be a multi-year project with associated costs.
  If the City Council provides direction to proceed with a comprehensive or
  focus update, and Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued to select a
  qualified consulting firm to work on the project and to work with staff to
  facilitate the process. Either concurrent or subsequent to selecting a
  qualified consulting firm, the City Council can also initiate the process to
  form an advisory committee.

  Alternative 1: Initiate a focus update and update elected elements in the
  General Plan. This can potentially be accomplished within a year’s time and
  the costs would be less than a comprehensive update. This City Council can
  prioritize which elements, such as adding an Environmental Justice Element
  to identify objectives and policies to reduce health risks to disadvantaged
  communities and promote food access, safe and sanitary homes, and
  physical activity, or updating the Safety Element to address risks associated
  with earthquakes, flooding, wildland, and urban fires.

  Alternative 2: Maintain the General Plan. This means all the policies and
  goals identified in the existing 2004 General Plan will remain the same with
  no changes until a future time.

  C. VALLEY BOULEVARD SPECIFIC PLAN AMENDMENT DISCUSSION

  On May 4, 2021, the Community Development Department provided an
  update to the City Council on the state of the local retail industry in San
  Gabriel, data on the impacts of the pandemic on sales tax, and efforts in
  place to assist existing and new businesses. On July 6, 2021, a follow up
  report was provided to the City Council to address requested supplemental
  information raised at the May 4th meeting. This report serves as a follow-up
  to the City Council’s direction to staff to initiate the process to amend the

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 2, 2024  9
   Valley Boulevard Specific Plan to allow ground floor office use. Additionally,
  Staff is seeking direction on establishing minimum densities within the
  Valley Boulevard Specific Plan area as outlined in Program 12 of the 2021-
  2029 Housing Element. There is no fiscal impact, this is an information item
  only.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council provide comments or directions on
  ground floor office use and establishing minimum densities.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members
  to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, July 16, 2024 at

  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website
